transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
On the sidelines of the APEC Summit of Pacific Rim Leaders in Shenzhen, China, President
Trump sounded optimistic, heading into a one-on-one meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
We've had a great relationship for many years.
We know each other for a long time.
And I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start, but I
think they'll come out of this.
Trump's meeting with Putin lasted about 40 minutes.
He is now meeting one-on-one with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
And then the three are to huddle together for a first-ever sit-down among the leaders
of the three countries.
Here's NPR's Deepa Shivaraj.
The Iran war remains a top global issue, particularly for Trump, so that's expected to come up in
this meeting.
Trump has been saying for weeks that he wants to discuss denuclearization with Xi and Putin
together.
Before this trip began, White House officials said that that was going to be the main topic
they wanted this meeting to be about, even though they know that China is not really
interested in talking about this issue with the U.S. and Russia.
The meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin is expected to begin shortly.
New York Congressman Hakeem Jeffries has been nominated for House Speaker when Democrats
take control of Congress in January, NPR's Claudia Grisellis reports.
House Democrats voted during a closed-door meeting 251 to 11 in support of Hakeem Jeffries'
nomination.
Afterwards, the current House Minority Leader told reporters his caucus will work to deliver
for the American people.
Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other, to fight MAGA extremism, and to get
big things done.
Several incoming, more left-wing House members who did not support Jeffries' bid said they're
still pushing for a more aggressive agenda to address affordability, immigration, and
other issues.
The House floor will hold its vote for Speaker on the first day of the new Congress next
year on January 3.
Claudia Grisellis, NPR News, the Capitol.
Japan's benchmark Nikkei is advancing, but Asian shares are largely down in Thursday
trading following a mixed day on Wall Street.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports Adele tumbled more than 1 percent while the tech-heavy NASDAQ
rose.
Blue chip stocks suffered, with Adele slumping more than 560 points.
Invidia shares also fell, despite a better-than-expected earnings report from the computer chip giant
on Tuesday.
A report from the Commerce Department on home-building activity shows a drop in permits last month
for future construction, high mortgage rates have been a drag on the housing market.
The Federal Reserve held short-term interest rates steady last month, but newly released
minutes from that meeting show most Fed policymakers expect further rate hikes will be necessary
to bring inflation under control.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Anthropics highly anticipated Wall Street debut is set for Thursday.
The company offering 825 million shares that will begin trading on the NASDAQ.
Anthropics has priced its initial public offering at $83 per share.
The proceeds expected to total some $81 billion, putting the company's IPO ahead of SpaceX,
which raised some $75 billion in June.
In Los Angeles, jurors are deliberating after hearing closing arguments in the retrial of
the man accused of setting a fire that eventually became last year's deadly Palisades fire.
Steve Futterman reports.
In closing arguments, prosecutors told jurors that Jonathan Rinderknecht was angry when
he allegedly started the Lochman fire just past midnight on New Year's Day last year.
That fire, they claim, was never completely put out and reemerged a week later as the
Palisades fire, which killed a dozen people and destroyed thousands of homes.
House attorney Steve Haney argued that the fire was started by New Year's celebrants
setting off fireworks.
It occurred right around midnight on New Year's, when that's one of the most active time for
fireworks in America.
So it's a logical inference.
In the first trial, jurors were split 10 to 2 in favor of acquittal.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman at the federal courthouse in Los Angeles.
Results from the midterm elections still coming in.
In Alaska, Republican Nick Begich has won re-election to the state's only House seat.
Begich was endorsed by President Trump in his race as one of the last to be called by
the Associated Press this election cycle.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Trump sounds optimistic at APEC summit in Shenzhen before meeting Putin one-on-one
Trump meets Putin for about 40 minutes, then meets Xi Jinping; three-way talks planned
House Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker, with some left-wing members pushing for more aggressive agenda
Asian shares mostly fall after mixed Wall Street session; Dow drops over 560 points
Commerce Department reports drop in building permits; Fed minutes signal possible rate hikes
Anthropic prices IPO at $83 per share, set to begin trading on NASDAQ Thursday
Los Angeles jury deliberates in retrial of Jonathan Rinderknecht over Palisades fire
Republican Nick Begich wins re-election to Alaska's only House seat
